title: Composite tool: overlay two entries live and erase the top one to reveal the one under it
description:
The composite shipped in MPI-362 is blind: the user selects two entries, one of them must ALREADY carry a mask, a modal asks Add or Subtract, and Sharp blends server-side. The user never sees the blend while deciding it. The user's redesign: selecting two entries overlays the FIRST over the SECOND on the canvas, and a brush/eraser pair edits the boundary live - the eraser removes the top image where it paints, revealing the entry underneath; the brush paints the top image back.

Delivery vehicle: a NEW composite tool in the rail (the user's own preferred option, over force-selecting an existing mask tool). It is a natural sibling of the mask family that MPI-371 just built - same strip, same brush/eraser/opacity, different meaning for the painted pixels.

Key design call to make in the brief: the erase layer IS a mask. If the tool paints into the same manual/subtract layer pair MaskManager already owns, Apply can hand that layer to the EXISTING /project/composite-media route as maskDataUrl and the whole server side stays untouched (full-res, no base64 round-trip for a 4K result). The new work is then the live two-image preview, not new pixel code.

BLAST RADIUS: js/components/Compounds/MpiHistoryList (the select-mode gate that currently requires a mask on one of the two entries - it must go), MpiGroupHistoryBlock.js `composite-requested` handler + `_runComposite` (~line 1706), MpiMaskCompositeDialog (Add/Subtract modal - kept or deleted, decide explicitly), MpiCanvasViewer + MpiCanvas/MaskManager (an underlay image layer that the base image is composited over), a new MpiToolOptionsComposite (register CSS in js/shell/preloadStyles.js AND props in js/components/types.js), MpiHistoryTools rail entry, docs/masking.md.
acceptance: Selecting two image entries offers Composite whether or not either one already carries a mask
The first-selected entry renders OVER the second on the canvas, both visible, before anything is committed
Eraser reveals the underlying entry live at the painted pixels; brush restores the top entry; brush size and opacity behave as in the mask family
Apply commits ONE new history entry through the existing full-res server composite path - no base64 round-trip of a 4K result
Leaving the tool or cancelling changes no history and no stored mask
The old mask-driven Add/Subtract dialog is kept or removed deliberately, with the decision recorded - not left dangling
Entries of differing pixel dimensions have a defined behaviour (fit, cover, or refuse) rather than an accident
